name: Vertex search
instructions:
### Rules

- `match` against an ARRAY of patterns is AND, not OR. To OR keywords, count the terms that hit:
  `count($terms[^.title match @ || pt::text(^.notes) match @ || ^.keyPoints[] match @]) > 0`
  Wildcard every term (`"cach*"`). Never match a multi-word phrase as one pattern.
  Measured here: `title match "cach*"` -> 4, `title match "fetch*"` -> 1,
  `title match ["cach*","fetch*"]` -> 0, the count-terms form -> 11.
- Do NOT use `text::semanticSimilarity()`. Embeddings are not enabled for this dataset and the query
  errors with `embeddingNotEnabledError`. Use wildcard keyword matching.
- `@ match text::query(...)` scores poorly here (1 result where keyword matching finds 11). Prefer
  the count-terms form above.
- Always project explicit fields. Never return whole documents.

### Schema notes

- A `lesson` does not store its parent course. Derive it with
  `*[_type == "course" && references(^._id)][0]`.
- `Module 5` and `Lesson 5.1` are positional, derived from `modules[]` and `modules[].lessons[]`
  order. There is no number field - do not look for one.
- `notes` is Portable Text. It cannot be text-matched directly; match `pt::text(notes)`.
- `duration` is in seconds.
- `modules` is an embedded object array on `course`, not its own document type.

### Video moments

- `video` documents are an internal lookup, never a result on their own. Always tie a matched moment
  back to the lesson whose `videoUrl` equals the video's `url`.
- Resolve a moment in two stages: match `chapters[].label` first, and fall back to `chunks[].text`
  only when no chapter matches.
- Never project a whole `chunks` or `chapters` array - it overflows the context window. Filter
  inside the projection and take at most three matches per video.
- Nearly every lesson video has a `video` document (118 of 120 today). About two thirds carry
  `chapters`; the rest are transcript-only, so falling back to `chunks[].text` is the NORMAL path,
  not an exception.
- A couple of lessons have no `video` document at all. For those, return the lesson without a
  timestamp rather than inventing one.
- `startSeconds` is an integer second on both arrays. Report it exactly as stored - never round it
  and never derive a second from a duration.

### Query patterns

- Lessons matching a learner's keywords, with the course derived:
  `*[_type == "lesson" && count($terms[^.title match @ || pt::text(^.notes) match @ || ^.keyPoints[] match @]) > 0]{ _id, title, keyPoints, "course": *[_type == "course" && references(^._id)][0].title }`
- Video moments, chapters and transcript in one pass, tied back to the lesson. Verified against this
  dataset:
  `*[_type == "video" && count($terms[^.chapters[].label match @ || ^.chunks[].text match @]) > 0]{ "lessonId": *[_type == "lesson" && videoUrl == ^.url][0]._id, "chapterMoments": chapters[count($terms[^.label match @]) > 0][0...3]{startSeconds, label}, "transcriptMoments": chunks[count($terms[^.text match @]) > 0][0...3]{startSeconds, text} }`
  Prefer a `chapterMoments` second; use `transcriptMoments` only when `chapterMoments` is empty.
- Scoping inside that nested filter matters. Within `$terms[...]`, `@` is the TERM and `^` is the
  chapter or chunk, so it is `^.label match @`. Measured here: `^.label match @` -> 3 matches,
  `@.label match ^.^` -> 0 matches on the same document.
